svg.title: DUET in four panels
svg.desc: Comic. 1: plain GRPO gives every prompt 8 rollouts that run until they stop by themselves; a solved prompt teaches nothing and a rambling rollout wastes thousands of tokens. 2: the Allocator gives more rollouts to half-right prompts, fewer to solved or long ones (rollouts proportional to disagreement over sqrt length). 3: the Stopper stops a rollout right after its boxed answer and cuts rollouts with no answer by the K2 deadline, except a random epsilon fraction that runs on with weight 1/epsilon to keep learning unbiased. 4: one conductor, the budget signal lambda*, keeps both on budget. Result: half the budget, 2.51x faster and +5.3 MATH-500 vs full-budget GRPO on Qwen3-1.7B.

g.text: 1 · Plain GRPO: the same effort for every prompt
8 rollouts for every prompt, and each one
runs until it stops by itself?!
Most of this compute teaches nothing.
2 · The Allocator: more rollouts where there is more to learn
most, so they get more rollouts.
3 · The Stopper: stop each rollout once its answer is in
Answer boxed? Stop right after it. No answer by K₂?
Cut it, except a random few (ε) that run on and count
4 · One conductor, λ*, keeps both on budget
Budget tight? I raise λ*: fewer
Half the budget → 2.51× faster, +5.3 MATH-500 vs. full GRPO
